shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus, one of the few emitters.

shadows.purpose: The ring while something is tuned in.

shadows.name: indicator-lit

shadows.name: pigment-dot
shadows.purpose: A shown category chip's dot, the markers' pigment; an emitter. Off when hidden.

shadows.name: marker-charge

shadows.purpose: Canvas marker glow by charge k (0..1).

motion.purpose: Title charge, mode rule, ring brightening.

motion.name: charge-title

motion.name: control

narrative.overview:
The globe is a glow-in-the-dark ceiling after lights-out. The room is matte night; the stories are phosphor marks on it. The one in the ring is fully charged, the ones you swept past keep a fading afterglow, so the globe remembers where you have looked. Everything a hand touches (buttons, sheets, fields) is unlit plastic: a flat dark fill and a hairline, never blurred, never glowing.

Light is the scarce resource and the whole hierarchy is built on it. Emitters are few and named: the tuned title, the ring, charged markers, keyboard focus, and two small lamps on the header's controls (the chosen mode's indicator light and the category chips' pigment dots, which are the markers' own pigment). Everything else is lit only by contrast with the dark. The reading surfaces (case and story pages, sheets) are the same room with the lamp off: Newsreader on night, mono labels on one scale, status shown by the form of a rule as well as its colour.

The world refuses two neighbours by construction: the Radio Garden clone (frosted panels, pill buttons, a boxed tuner card) and the neon HUD (glowing edges, scanlines, coloured shadows on chrome). It is calm and even-handed, campfire rather than jump scare.
keyCharacteristics: One emitted light, phosphor, plus the pinned category pigments on the globe.
Only emitters glow: tuned title, ring, charged markers, focus, the mode indicator light and the chip dots.
Controls are unlit plastic: flat plate, 1px hairline, no blur, no lit fill.
Newsreader for anything read; IBM Plex Mono for interface, on one label scale and one control size.
Case status by form and colour: solid, dashed, dotted.
The pointer-following eyeball is the logo, spanning a two-line lockup: the name in phosphor serif capitals without glow, an italic line beneath.

rules.name: The Single Emitter Rule
rules.body: Phosphor is the only light the interface emits. New accents are pigments (category, status), never a second glow colour.

rules.name: The Pinned Pigments Rule
rules.body: Category colours come only from `src/lib/categories.ts` and canvas/preview copies of the palette only from `src/lib/tokens.ts`, kept in sync with `tokens.css` by `tokens.test.ts`. No hex or `rgba()` outside `tokens.css` in CSS.

rules.name: The One Label Scale Rule
rules.body: Every small-capital label uses `--label-size` and `--label-track`; every control uses `--control-size`. No third size, no per-component tracking.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a title. A page or sheet opens with its title; category, place, date and status follow beneath it in the meta line. Mono label headings ("What was reported") are the section heading itself, never a kicker over a serif heading.

rules.name: The Lockup Sizes Rule
rules.body: The wordmark's sizes belong to the logo, not to the text ramp: the name (Wordmark, 20px) and the tagline (Wordmark Tagline, italic 14px), dropping to a 16px name (0.11em) on phones and a 13.5px name (0.06em) with the tagline hidden when the header carries five buttons. Never reuse them for headings or body text.

rules.name: The Only Emitters Glow Rule
rules.body: The tuned title, the ring, charged markers, focus, the mode switch's indicator light and the chip pigment dots are the only things that give off light. Panels, buttons, chip and segment containers, body text and borders never glow.

rules.name: The Unlit Plastic Rule
rules.body: Controls are a flat fill and a 1px hairline. No backdrop blur, no lit fills, no glowing borders. A pressed or primary control is set apart by phosphor text and a phosphor-dim rule; the chosen segment of a switch is raised with the Highlight wash, phosphor text and its lit indicator.

rules.name: The Charge Rule
rules.body: A marker's light is its charge: the tuned marker charges fully in about 0.14s, markers passing within 90px pick up at most 60%, and all charge decays as afterglow (to a third in about 4s). With reduced motion, the tuned marker is simply lit and the rest are not; the title shows its charged state without the charge animation.

rules.name: The Form Carries Status Rule
rules.body: Case status is shown by the border form as well as colour: solid for Unexplained, dashed for Disputed, dotted for Explained. Finer labels (Confirmed, Mostly explained) take the form of the status they belong to. A hidden category chip goes dashed (Line Strong), transparent and muted, with a hollow dot: the same form language as the pills.

dos: Do reserve light for emitters: the tuned title (`--emit-text`), the ring, charged markers and focus.
Do build controls from `--plate` or `--night-2`, a `--line` hairline and `--radius` (8px); mark pressed or primary with phosphor text and `--phosphor-dim` rule.
Do use `--label-size` / `--label-track` for every small-capital label and `--control-size` for every control.
Do show case status by border form as well as colour: solid unexplained, dashed disputed, dotted explained.
Do draw icons from the SVG `Icon` set in `src/components/brand.tsx`, with `aria-hidden` and `currentColor`.
Do keep static charged and uncharged states under reduced motion, on canvas and in CSS.
Do set reading in Newsreader and interface in IBM Plex Mono.
donts: Don't glow panels, buttons, chip or switch containers, borders or body text, and don't use coloured shadows on chrome.
Don't use backdrop blur, frosted glass, pill-shaped buttons or a boxed tuner card.
Don't fill a control with phosphor or a pigment to show it is on.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a title.
Don't use text glyphs (arrows, crosses, ticks) as icons.
Don't add a third label size or per-component letter-spacing.
Don't write hex or `rgba()` outside `tokens.css`, or hard-code category colours outside `categories.ts`.
Don't draw country borders on any globe.
